# Support Call Without Recap

`customer_support.sit.support_call_no_recap` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

Owned by `customer_support.customer_communication.proactive_status_updates`


> A call with the customer happened and nothing was written afterwards. The gap is not courtesy, it is custody: everything established on that call — what was reproduced, what was ruled out, what we said we would do next and by when — currently exists only as two people's recollection, and one of those people is going to be replaced by a colleague on the next shift. The recap is what converts a synchronous hour into a durable record, and it is also the customer's only chance to correct our understanding before we act on it. The expert discipline is that it goes out the same working day, in the customer's language rather than the engineer's, and that it separates what was OBSERVED from what was CONCLUDED — because the conclusion is the part most likely to be wrong and the part they can most usefully challenge.


## Layer 2 binding

The join that makes this situation reachable. An unbound situation never compiles, and nothing errors when it doesn't.

- `meeting_no_followup`

> Of the signal lists, only followup_sent is in the substrate today. minutes_circulated is an admin-pack planned kind reused here because a support recap is the same act; callback_promised, reproduction_confirmed, agent_reassigned, escalation_requested and angry_language are support-native planned kinds. These lists are unvalidated, so the mixture is legal — recorded here rather than left for a reader to discover.
THE KNOWN IMPRECISION. meeting_no_followup cannot tell a support call from a QBR, an internal standup or a sales demo, because Layer 2 has no notion of what a meeting was FOR. Today the narrowing above is the best available and it is weak. The clean fix is not a new situation type but a meeting classification on the L1 side — until then this situation over-fires on calendars belonging to people who both sell and support, which is most of a small company. agent_reassigned appears under decay rather than progress on purpose: a reassignment before the recap is written is the exact moment the diagnosis is lost, and treating it as neutral workflow is how it stays invisible.
